name: GratisAI Index dataset
description: Free and open-source AI tools with the pricing label we verified, a one-line reason for that label, and the date it was checked against the vendor page.

fields.pricing_model: One of: 100% Free, Generous Free Tier, Limited Free Tier, Open Source, Free Trial. Definitions: https://gratisai.com.au/methodology
fields.pricing_reasoning: Why the tool carries that label, with the published limits where they exist.
fields.last_verified: ISO date the entry was last checked against the vendor pricing or docs page.
fields.sources: Vendor pages the label was based on.

tools.name: Freebuff
tools.tagline: Open-source multi-agent coding agent & app builder with CLI, desktop, and cloud sandboxes
tools.description: Freebuff is an open-source, multi-agent AI coding assistant and full-stack app builder positioned as a free alternative to Claude Code, Cursor, and Devin. No API key or credit card is required: advertising funds a daily allowance of usage hours, and optional paid plans add hours and models. Specialized sub-agents handle context gathering, planning, editing, and automated testing across CLI, Desktop, and Cloud environments.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan costs $0 with no card and refills 30 hours of model usage daily with unlimited messages per session; paid plans start at $8/month.
pros: No credit card or API key required; ads fund the free daily hours
Multi-agent architecture divides tasks between planning, coding, and review
Open-source CLI, agents, and SDK under Apache 2.0 on GitHub
cons: Free usage is metered in daily hours that vary by country

tools.name: Bolt.new by StackBlitz
tools.tagline: Prompt, build, run, and deploy full-stack web applications directly in the browser
tools.description: Bolt.new leverages WebContainers to run a full Node.js environment directly in your browser tab. Prompt the AI to build complete full-stack React, Next.js, Vue, or Svelte applications with live package installation, hot-reload terminal, and instant deployment.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free forever, no card: 1M tokens/month with a 300K daily cap, 3 collaborators and hosting; Pro is $25/month for 10M tokens and a custom domain.
pros: Runs complete Node.js environments and npm packages in-browser
Live interactive preview updates in real-time as the agent codes
Generous free daily token allocation for building full apps
cons: Requires internet access to stream model tokens

tools.name: OpenHands (All-Hands AI)
tools.tagline: Open-source autonomous AI software development agent capable of complex engineering
tools.description: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin) is the flagship open-source autonomous software engineering platform. It can write code, run terminal commands, fix bugs, read pull requests, and browse the web inside secure Docker environments.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed agent you self-host with your own LLM key, so there is no vendor allowance and no card; cloud offers a free $10 credit then Teams at $500/month.
pros: 100% open-source under MIT with 40k+ GitHub stars
Runs entirely in Docker with isolated execution sandboxes
Pairs with local Ollama models or free API endpoints
cons: Docker setup required for local containerized orchestration

tools.name: Lovable.dev
tools.tagline: Full-stack software engineer agent turning ideas into real apps with Supabase & GitHub sync
tools.description: Lovable is a generative web app builder that crafts frontend and backend logic with natural language. Generates clean React code with Tailwind CSS, connects directly to Supabase for authentication and database storage, and pushes commits to GitHub.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free needs no card but limits builds to 5 per day and 30 per month with 20 cloud credits, which fits prototyping rather than shipping.
pros: Automated database and authentication wiring with Supabase
Direct GitHub synchronization with clean git commits
Generous starter credits to build and deploy prototypes
cons: Monthly free credit limit applies to heavy iteration loops

tools.name: Aider
tools.tagline: Leading open-source AI pair programmer for terminal and git-integrated app development
tools.description: Aider allows you to build and edit codebases using conversational AI directly from your command line. It edits files across multi-module projects, automatically creates git commits with descriptive messages, and pairs with local Ollama or cloud models.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 terminal pair programmer with no account or card; you supply your own API key or local model, so usage is billed by your provider.
pros: Industry benchmark leader in automated git commits and multi-file refactoring
Works offline with Ollama (DeepSeek Coder / Qwen 2.5)
Permissive Apache 2.0 license with active maintainers
cons: Command-line interface only (no graphical drag-and-drop)

tools.name: GPT Engineer
tools.tagline: Specify what you want to build and the AI constructs the entire codebase
tools.description: GPT Engineer adapts to your style, asks clarifying questions when requirements are ambiguous, and constructs complete multi-file project repositories with documentation, tests, and configuration. The project is now archived, so treat it as a reference implementation rather than an actively maintained tool.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed CLI you install yourself; there is no hosted tier and no card, but it needs your own model API key, so you pay for tokens.
pros: Generates complete folder hierarchies and multi-file architectures in 1 run
Asks interactive clarifying questions before writing code
Over 50k GitHub stars with vibrant community extensions
cons: Requires careful prompt specification for large production systems
Repository is archived and no longer receives updates

tools.name: Dyad
tools.tagline: Free, local, open-source AI app builder that runs on your own machine
tools.description: Dyad is an open-source desktop app builder that generates full-stack React applications locally, keeping code and prompts on your computer. It supports bring-your-own model keys or local models via Ollama, offers live preview, and exports clean code with no subscription.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free app runs locally with no account or card and gives 20 agent messages a day; code is Apache-2.0 apart from the pro directory; Pro is $20/month.
pros: Runs locally with your own keys or local Ollama models
No subscription credits or per-prompt metering
Apache 2.0 with full code export
cons: You must supply a model key or run a local model
Smaller template ecosystem than cloud builders

tools.name: Onlook
tools.tagline: Open-source visual editor that writes React and Tailwind code into your project
tools.description: Onlook is a visual-first editor for React apps: click elements in a live preview, prompt a change, and the agent edits your actual codebase with Tailwind classes. The desktop app runs locally against your own repository, so the design and the code stay in sync.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 editor that the vendor says can be self-hosted free; the hosted cloud is quoted per team with no published free allowance.
pros: Edits real React and Tailwind code instead of exporting mockups
Local desktop app works against your own repository
Apache 2.0 with an active community
cons: Cloud version has paid tiers; self-hosting is the free path
Best suited to React projects only

tools.name: Ollama
tools.tagline: Get up and running with Llama 3, DeepSeek, and Mistral locally in one command
tools.description: Ollama allows developers to run open-source large language models entirely locally on macOS, Linux, and Windows. It features a streamlined CLI, built-in REST API, and support for quantized GGUF weights with GPU acceleration across Apple Silicon, CUDA, and ROCm.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT app: running models on your own hardware is unlimited and needs no card; the optional cloud is pay-as-you-go per token with 3 concurrent requests.
pros: Zero telemetry and 100% private local inference
One-command installation with instant model downloads
OpenAI-compatible REST API endpoint out of the box
cons: Requires substantial unified memory for 70B parameter models

tools.name: v0 by Vercel
tools.tagline: Generative UI system to build React, Next.js, and Tailwind CSS components
tools.description: v0 creates production-ready frontend components, web pages, and full-stack layouts using natural language prompts. It outputs standard React code with Tailwind CSS that can be copied directly into any codebase.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free gives new users $5 of one-time credits and 7 messages a day, with no card required; Plus is $30/user/month including $30 of credits.
pros: Generates clean TypeScript code using modern Tailwind CSS
Live interactive preview and responsive viewport testing
Generous recurring monthly free generations
cons: Rate-limited on complex multi-page iterations on free plan

tools.name: DeepSeek Chat & Coder
tools.tagline: State-of-the-art open-weights reasoning and code intelligence model
tools.description: DeepSeek provides high-capability reasoning and coding models with open weights and a completely free web chat and mobile app. There is no paid consumer subscription. Recognized for strong code generation, mathematical reasoning, and low inference latency; the developer API is billed per token rather than free.
tools.pricing_reasoning: The consumer chat is free with no paid plan and no card, and the vendor publishes no usage cap; API access is billed separately per million tokens.
pros: Rivals frontier proprietary models in code benchmarks
Completely free web chat without credit limits
Permissive open-weights release for self-hosting
cons: Occasional peak-hour server queue during major releases

tools.name: Continue.dev
tools.tagline: Open-source AI code assistant extension for VS Code and JetBrains
tools.description: Continue is the leading open-source copilot that plugs directly into VS Code and JetBrains IDEs. Connect any local model (via Ollama or LM Studio) or cloud provider for inline autocomplete, codebase chat, and refactoring.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 extension you point at your own model or keys; the hosted pricing lists only paid per-token plans, with no free tier to rely on.
pros: Works completely offline when connected to Ollama
Full codebase indexing and retrieval augmented context
Zero vendor lock-in; switch models in 1 click
cons: Requires configuring model endpoints for best performance

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.tagline: Discover, download, and run local LLMs with a polished desktop GUI
tools.description: LM Studio makes running local open-source models as simple as clicking a button. Browse Hugging Face GGUF models directly within the application, run hardware-accelerated chat, and expose a local OpenAI-compatible server.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free desktop app runs local models through llama.cpp and MLX with no card and no usage cap; paid tiers only add cloud models and start at $20/month.
pros: Intuitive desktop GUI with automatic GPU offloading detection
Direct search and download from Hugging Face model repository
Built-in local developer server with API testing playground
cons: Core application is closed-source freeware, though model weights are OSS

tools.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf & Codeium)
tools.tagline: Agentic code editor with unlimited Tab completions and inline edits on the free plan
tools.description: Codeium became Windsurf in 2025 and was renamed Devin Desktop by Cognition in June 2026; codeium.com and windsurf.com now redirect here. The free plan keeps the unlimited Tab completions and inline edits that made Codeium popular, adds a light quota for agent work with a restricted model list, and runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free $0 plan has no published numbers, only a light agent quota and limited model access, alongside unlimited tab completions; Pro is $20/month.
pros: Unlimited Tab completions and inline edits even on the free plan
Full agentic editor with a light free quota for agent tasks
No time limit on the free tier; Pro is optional at $20/month
cons: Free plan restricts model choice and caps agent usage

tools.name: Google Antigravity
tools.tagline: Agent-first IDE, desktop app and CLI from Google, free with a Google account
tools.description: Google Antigravity is the agent-first development platform that replaced Gemini CLI for individual accounts on 18 June 2026. It combines a desktop app, IDE extensions and the Antigravity CLI on one agent harness that can run several agents in parallel, with scheduled tasks and Gemini 3.8 Flash as the core agent model. The individual plan costs nothing and needs no credit card; usage is metered against a quota that refreshes weekly, and Google does not publish it as a fixed request count.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Individual plan is $0 with no card and unlimited tab completions, but the agent quota is described only as meaningful and refreshed weekly, so no figure can be planned around.
pros: No subscription and no credit card for the individual plan
One agent harness across desktop app, IDE extensions and the CLI
Unlimited tab completions on every plan, including free
cons: Closed source, unlike the Apache 2.0 Gemini CLI it replaced
Free quota is not published as a fixed number and refreshes weekly
No bring-your-own-key option for extra quota

tools.name: Goose
tools.tagline: Open-source local AI agent that automates coding and desktop workflows
tools.description: Goose is an open-source, extensible AI agent that runs locally and connects to the tools you already use through MCP extensions. It writes code, runs commands, manages files, and automates workflows using local models or your own API keys.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 local agent with no card; it has no allowance of its own, so you fund it with provider credits or a model free tier.
pros: Runs entirely on your machine with local or bring-your-own models
MCP extension system connects to real tools
Apache 2.0 and backed by Block
cons: Configuration is more involved than hosted agents
Requires a model provider or local runtime

tools.name: ComfyUI
tools.tagline: Modular node-based GUI and backend for Stable Diffusion and Flux
tools.description: ComfyUI is the definitive node-based graphic interface for generative image synthesis. Build modular pipelines for txt2img, inpainting, ControlNet, IP-Adapter, and upscale workflows with precise execution graphs.
tools.pricing_reasoning: GPL-3.0 and free for local graph execution with no card; credits only apply to partner nodes and cloud, where five runs are free.
pros: Unmatched control over generative diffusion graphs
Extremely memory efficient compared to traditional WebUIs
Thriving open-source custom node ecosystem
cons: Steeper learning curve for node-based graph composition

tools.name: Recraft.ai
tools.tagline: Generate clean vector SVGs, 3D icons, and brand graphics with daily credits
tools.description: Recraft is a specialized design canvas that generates editable vector SVG graphics, isometric 3D illustrations, and digital art with consistent brand color palettes. Free tier includes daily generative credits.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan needs no card and allows up to 30 generations a day on daily-resetting credits, with 3 uploads a day and 2 images per prompt, for non-commercial use.
pros: Exports true scalable vectors (SVG) with clean node paths
Precise style palette matching across illustration sets
Free daily credits are enough for icon and illustration experiments
cons: Free-tier images are public and non-commercial; credits are limited

tools.name: Krita AI Diffusion
tools.tagline: Generative AI painting plugin integrated natively into the open-source Krita canvas
tools.description: Bring generative inpainting, outpainting, and real-time live drawing directly into Krita. Connects to local ComfyUI backends to paint with AI guidance without leaving the digital painting canvas.
tools.pricing_reasoning: GPL-3.0 plugin that runs locally on your own GPU through a ComfyUI backend; there is no hosted tier, no allowance and no card.
pros: Runs 100% locally with zero cloud dependencies
Interactive real-time canvas preview as you sketch
Preserves layer blending modes and artistic control
cons: Requires pre-installed Krita and a local GPU server

tools.name: InvokeAI
tools.tagline: Self-hosted studio for Stable Diffusion and Flux with a professional canvas
tools.description: InvokeAI is an open-source generative image studio with a unified canvas, layer-based inpainting, control layers, and workflow support, running on your own GPU. It installs via Docker or Python and exposes a local API.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 app you self-host on your own GPU or Apple Silicon; there is no paid tier or card, and hosted GPUs come from third parties.
pros: Professional canvas with layers and regional control
Runs fully local on your own GPU
Apache 2.0 with a steady release cadence
cons: Requires a capable GPU for comfortable use
Initial model setup takes time

tools.name: Upscayl
tools.tagline: Free, offline AI image upscaler for desktop
tools.description: Upscayl enlarges and restores images locally using Real-ESRGAN and other open models, with batch processing and no uploads. It is a free desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux with no account or credit system.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Desktop app is free, open source and local with no limits or card; the optional cloud gives a 10-credit trial then charges $24.99 per 300 credits.
pros: Fully offline; images never leave your machine
Batch upscaling with several open models
No account, credits, or watermark
cons: AGPL-3.0 license affects redistribution
GPU recommended for large batches

tools.name: Claude.ai
tools.tagline: Nuanced writing, reasoning, and document analysis on Claude's free plan
tools.description: Anthropic's conversational assistant, used on a free daily allowance without a card. Renowned for natural human-like prose, strong context comprehension, the Artifacts interactive preview pane, and code assistance. Paid tiers raise message caps and unlock the newest models.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan is $0 with no card and includes Projects up to 5, but usage is limited every 5 hours and every week with no message count published.
pros: Exceptional literary quality, tone balance, and nuance
Artifacts pane renders interactive React apps and SVG graphics
Upload PDFs, research papers, and spreadsheets for free
cons: Strict message caps per 4-hour window on free accounts

tools.name: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)
tools.tagline: AI research notebook grounded in your own sources, with Audio and Video Overviews
tools.description: Renamed from NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook in July 2026, this free Google tool grounds every answer in the notes, PDFs, Docs, and YouTube transcripts you upload. It produces citation-backed summaries, Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, slide decks, and mind maps on a free tier of 100 notebooks and 50 sources each.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free with a Google account and no card: 100 notebooks, 50 sources per notebook, 50 chats a day, 3 audio overviews a day and 10 reports a day.
pros: 100% free with generous source upload limits
Zero hallucination due to strict document-grounded citations
Groundbreaking Audio Overview creates natural conversational podcasts
cons: Limited to analyzing uploaded sources rather than open web search

tools.name: Google Gemini (AI Studio free tier)
tools.tagline: Free API access to Gemini Flash models with multimodal input and long context
tools.description: Google AI Studio offers a standing free tier on the Gemini API with no credit card. Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite and other Flash models are listed as free of charge for input and output on the free tier, with multimodal input and long context. Rate limits are set per project and per model and are shown in AI Studio rather than as one published number. Free-tier prompts are used to improve Google products, which is the main reason not to send confidential material through it.
tools.pricing_reasoning: The API free tier is priced at free of charge and needs only a project, but per-model daily quotas are shown inside AI Studio rather than on the pricing page.
pros: Standing free tier with no billing account required
Flash and Flash-Lite input and output are free of charge on the free tier
High inference speed suitable for real-time applications
cons: Free-tier prompts may be used to improve Google products
Pro and flagship models are paid only

tools.name: ChatGPT Free
tools.tagline: Everyday conversational intelligence, web browsing, and data analysis at no cost
tools.description: OpenAI's free tier runs its fast Luna model (GPT-6 Luna rolling out from October 2026) with unlimited everyday text chats. Web search, data analysis, file and image uploads, image creation, custom GPTs, and 500 MB of Library storage are included under separate per-tool caps, with no subscription or card required.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free account needs no card and allows unlimited everyday text chats under abuse safeguards, with 500 MB of Library storage; media and research have separate limits.
pros: Unlimited everyday text chats on the free tier
Live web search, data analysis, and image creation included
Extensive ecosystem of pre-configured custom GPTs
cons: Uploads, images, voice, and deep research are capped per tool
Ads may appear on the free tier in some countries

tools.name: LibreChat
tools.tagline: Self-hosted, multi-model chat UI with agents, MCP tools, and code interpreter
tools.description: LibreChat is an open-source ChatGPT-style interface that connects OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and local models in one place. It adds conversation search, agents, MCP tools, file handling, and multi-user access, all self-hosted.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed chat UI you self-host with no subscription and no card; it ships without keys, so you add your own provider key or a local model.
pros: One interface for cloud and local models
Agents, MCP tools, and file search built in
MIT licensed and actively maintained
cons: You supply model API keys or a local runtime
Multi-user setups need a Docker deployment

tools.name: Open Notebook
tools.tagline: Open-source notebook that grounds answers in your own sources, with audio overviews
tools.description: Open Notebook turns PDFs, links, and notes into a private research notebook with grounded chat, summaries, and podcast-style audio overviews. It runs locally and supports many model providers, so sources never leave your infrastructure.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed notebook you run yourself in Docker with no card; it needs your own model key or a local Ollama model, and has no paid tier.
pros: Private alternative to NotebookLM with local storage
Audio overviews and citation-backed chat
MIT licensed with pluggable model providers
cons: Requires Docker plus API keys or local models
Less polished than the hosted original

tools.name: Kokoro TTS
tools.tagline: Open-source 82M parameter text-to-speech model with natural human cadence
tools.description: Kokoro is a breakthrough lightweight open-source text-to-speech model (82 million parameters) capable of synthesizing expressive, natural speech in English, Japanese, French, and Spanish with minimal compute overhead.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 weights for an 82M-parameter TTS model you run locally with no card; hosted APIs bill around $0.06 per hour of audio and publish no free quota.
pros: Incredible audio quality for an 82M parameter model
Runs faster than real-time on standard laptop CPUs
Permissive Apache 2.0 license for commercial & personal use
cons: CLI / Python setup required for custom voice blending

tools.name: OpenAI Whisper
tools.tagline: General-purpose speech recognition and multilingual transcription model
tools.description: Whisper is an open-source neural net trained on 680,000 hours of multilingual and multitask supervised data collected from the web. It delivers robust automatic speech recognition (ASR) and language translation.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT licence covers code and weights; it runs locally with no paid tier, credits or card, and small models transcribe on CPU.
pros: Industry benchmark for transcription accuracy and accents
Runs 100% offline with zero cloud audio leakage
Wide community tooling ecosystem (whisper.cpp, MacWhisper)

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.tagline: Lifelike speech synthesis, emotional AI voices, and sound effects generator
tools.description: ElevenLabs produces some of the most realistic human voice generation available. The free tier grants 10,000 credits per month (roughly 10 minutes of speech), shared across text-to-speech, speech-to-text, sound effects, voice design, and music, with no credit card required.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan is $0 with no card and gives 10k credits a month, about 10 minutes of speech, plus 3 Studio projects and no commercial licence.
pros: Unsurpassed emotional range and pacing in voice output
Clean audio generation for podcasts, games, and video voiceovers
Monthly free character allowance resets automatically
cons: Instant voice cloning requires paid tier
Free-plan audio is non-commercial and requires crediting ElevenLabs

tools.name: Suno AI
tools.tagline: Generate complete studio-quality songs with vocals and instrumentation
tools.description: Suno produces full 2-minute songs with vocals, lyrics, and instrumentals in any genre from jazz to synthwave. Provides 50 free credits every day (equivalent to 10 song generations) on the free tier.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan is $0 forever with no card and gives 50 credits a day, enough for about 10 songs, renewing daily; downloads and commercial rights need a paid plan.
pros: Daily 50 credits allow regular experimentation without payment
High musicality with diverse instrumentation and vocal styles
Generate from custom lyrics or prompt themes
cons: Free-plan songs are personal use only with no commercial rights
Free accounts have no monthly downloads and use the v6-mini model

tools.name: Piper TTS
tools.tagline: Fast, lightweight neural text-to-speech that runs on a Raspberry Pi
tools.description: Piper is a fast local neural text-to-speech engine built on VITS and designed for low-resource hardware. It ships dozens of voices across many languages and runs offline from the command line or Python with near real-time synthesis on a CPU.
tools.pricing_reasoning: GPL-3.0 engine installed with pip that runs offline on CPU with no card or paid tier; voice model rights vary by model card.
pros: Faster than real time on a plain CPU
Dozens of voices across many languages
Completely offline with no account
cons: GPL-3.0 licensing for redistribution
Voice quality below large cloud models

tools.name: F5-TTS
tools.tagline: Open-source voice cloning and text-to-speech with natural prosody
tools.description: F5-TTS is a flow-matching text-to-speech model that clones a voice from a short reference clip and synthesises natural speech in English and Chinese. It runs locally on GPU or CPU and ships with a Gradio interface and CLI.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Code is MIT and the pretrained models are CC-BY-NC; you run it on your own GPU with no card, no hosted tier and no credits.

MIT licensed with checkpoints on Hugging Face
Local inference keeps audio private
cons: GPU strongly recommended for fast synthesis
Only English and Chinese are well supported

tools.name: ACE-Step
tools.tagline: Open-source music generation model for full songs with vocals
tools.description: ACE-Step is an open music foundation model that generates complete tracks, including vocals and instrumentation, from lyrics and style prompts. It runs locally, supports LoRA fine-tunes, and is fast enough to iterate on a single GPU.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 music model with weights on Hugging Face, self-hosted through pip, Docker or ComfyUI on your own GPU; no hosted tier or card.
pros: Full-song generation with vocals, free and local
Apache 2.0 with LoRA training support
Fast inference compared with similar models
cons: Needs a modern GPU and several GB of VRAM
Quality varies by genre and prompt

tools.name: Tripo3D
tools.tagline: Generate textured 3D meshes from text prompts or 2D images in seconds
tools.description: Tripo3D converts text prompts or single 2D images into textured 3D models with downloadable GLB and FBX formats. Free tier includes monthly credits to generate, inspect, and export meshes.

Clean export to GLB, OBJ, and USDZ for Three.js/Blender
Generous free starter credits

tools.name: Wan 2.2

tools.description: Wan 2.2 is Alibaba's open-weights video generation family, covering text-to-video, image-to-video, and speech-to-video with a mixture-of-experts architecture. The weights are downloadable and runnable locally through ComfyUI or the reference code.

pros: Open weights under Apache 2.0 for local generation
Strong motion quality for an open model
Drops straight into ComfyUI pipelines
cons: Large VRAM requirements for full-quality output
Setup is technical compared with hosted tools

tools.name: LTX-Video
tools.tagline: Fast open-weights video model that generates clips faster than real time
tools.description: LTX-Video from Lightricks is an open-weights diffusion transformer that produces short video clips quickly, with text-to-video and image-to-video modes. It runs locally and integrates with ComfyUI and Diffusers.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 repository and weights you run locally on an NVIDIA GPU; the separate LTX Studio app gives 800 one-time credits.
pros: Generation speed well above most open video models
Runs on consumer GPUs
Active ComfyUI and Diffusers integration
cons: Custom open-weights license rather than Apache or MIT
Clip length and resolution are limited

tools.name: Hunyuan3D 2.x
tools.tagline: Open-weights image-to-3D model that produces textured meshes
tools.description: Hunyuan3D from Tencent converts a single image into a textured 3D mesh with a two-stage shape and texture pipeline. The weights are downloadable, runnable locally from Python, and export to standard mesh formats.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Tencent community licence, unavailable in the EU, UK and South Korea and needing a separate licence above 1M monthly users; self-hosted with no card.
pros: Free local image-to-3D with downloadable weights
Good texture quality for an open pipeline
Exports usable meshes for DCC tools
cons: Tencent community license, not a standard OSI license
Significant GPU memory and setup time

tools.name: Meshy
tools.tagline: Text and image to 3D cloud generator with a no-card free tier
tools.description: Meshy generates textured 3D assets from text prompts or reference images in the browser, with PBR textures and game-engine-ready exports. The free plan includes 100 monthly credits and 10 downloads of untextured Meshy 6 Lite models, with no credit card required.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan needs no card and gives 100 credits a month for up to 10 assets, with 10 downloads a month of Meshy 6 Lite only and CC BY 4.0 output.
pros: 100 free credits every month with no card
Fast cloud generation with no GPU needed
Exports GLB, FBX, OBJ, and USDZ
cons: Free downloads limited to 10 untextured Meshy 6 Lite models
Free output is CC BY 4.0 and requires attribution

tools.name: Perplexity AI
tools.tagline: AI search engine delivering synthesized answers with real-time web citations
tools.description: Perplexity combines conversational LLMs with live web indexing to deliver direct answers backed by verifiable source citations. Free tier offers unlimited standard searches and recurring Pro search queries.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free needs no card and gives 3 Pro searches a day and 1 research query a month, with basic searches effectively unlimited.
pros: Unlimited quick searches with accurate numbered citations
Focused modes for Academic papers, YouTube, and Reddit
Collections feature organizes research projects neatly
cons: Pro searches (deep research) limited on free plan

tools.name: Elicit
tools.tagline: Automated literature review and empirical research synthesis for researchers
tools.description: Elicit searches more than 138 million academic papers and 545,000 clinical trials to answer research questions, extract methodology details, and build literature review tables. The free Basic plan includes unlimited paper search, summaries, and chat with full-text papers, with limited Research Agent and report usage.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Basic is free with no card and includes unlimited search across more than 138 million papers plus unlimited summaries, but only 2 research reports a month.
pros: Extracts sample sizes, methodologies, and outcomes across papers
High research rigor with direct DOI paper references
Free Basic plan with unlimited paper search and summaries
cons: Complex multi-column systematic synthesis consumes credits

tools.name: Open WebUI
tools.tagline: User-friendly, extensible web interface for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs
tools.description: Open WebUI is the leading self-hosted, offline-first ChatGPT alternative. Connects to Ollama, LM Studio, or external APIs with full chat history, document RAG, image generation integration, and multi-user RBAC.
tools.pricing_reasoning: BSD-3 community edition is free for unlimited users with no card; it needs your own server and model keys, and a branding clause applies at 50 or more users.
pros: Feature parity with ChatGPT Plus in a self-hosted package
Built-in document vector search and retrieval (RAG)
Source-available under the Open WebUI License, actively developed
cons: Requires Docker setup to host locally

tools.name: Semantic Scholar
tools.tagline: Free non-profit academic search across 200M+ papers, with an open API
tools.description: Semantic Scholar is a research engine from the Allen Institute for AI that indexes hundreds of millions of papers with citation context, TLDR summaries, and author metrics. Web search and the public API are free, with no account needed for basic use.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free account and free API with no paid tier or card; keyed access is limited to 1 request per second over a corpus of 214 million papers.
pros: Genuinely free, non-profit academic search
Citation graphs and TLDR summaries
Public API for scripts and research tooling
cons: No conversational AI layer like newer research assistants
API rate limits apply without a key

tools.name: Consensus
tools.tagline: AI research search that answers questions from peer-reviewed studies
tools.description: Consensus searches scientific literature and synthesises answers backed by peer-reviewed papers, with a consensus meter showing how far studies agree. The free tier includes unlimited paper searches, 10 Pro messages, and 3 Deep reviews per month.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free needs no card and gives unlimited paper searches plus 10 Pro messages, 3 deep reviews, 10 study snapshots and 30 API calls a month.
pros: Unlimited paper searches on the free tier
Consensus meter summarises agreement across studies
Cites peer-reviewed sources only
cons: AI analysis capped at 10 Pro messages and 3 Deep reviews monthly
Full-text access still depends on publisher paywalls

tools.name: n8n Community Edition
tools.tagline: Self-hosted workflow automation platform with AI agent nodes and LangChain
tools.description: n8n is a visual workflow automation platform that connects 400+ services with native AI agent nodes, vector stores, and custom LLM prompts. The self-hosted Community Edition is completely free.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Self-hosted Community edition is free indefinitely with no execution cap under the Sustainable Use License; the cloud free option is only a 14-day trial.
pros: Unlimited workflow executions when self-hosted on your server
Native AI Agent nodes with tool calling and memory stores
Massive library of 400+ integrations and community templates
cons: Fair-code license has restrictions on selling n8n as a hosted service

tools.name: Flowise
tools.tagline: Open-source drag & drop UI to build customized LLM chains and autonomous agents
tools.description: Flowise provided an intuitive visual canvas to build LangChain workflows, autonomous agents, and RAG pipelines without writing code. The project was archived in August 2026 and reached end of life, so self-hosted installs keep running but no longer receive fixes; the Apache 2.0 code remains forkable.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 core you self-host with your own infrastructure and keys; the repository now states it has been archived, so no new development is expected.
pros: Visual node interface makes complex agent logic transparent
One-command npm or Docker installation
Permissive Apache 2.0 license
cons: Archived in August 2026 with no further security fixes
Advanced production deployments require custom state management
tools.scope_caveat: Scope note: the Flowise repository is archived, so the project is no longer actively developed. The entry is kept because self-hosting still works, but it is a removal candidate.

tools.name: Dify.ai
tools.tagline: Open-source LLM app development platform combining AI workflow orchestration and RAG
tools.description: Dify is an open-source development platform that orchestrates LLM applications from prototype to production. Features a visual prompt studio, comprehensive RAG pipeline, and autonomous multi-agent execution.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Community edition self-hosts free with no licence required; the cloud sandbox gives 200 message credits, 1 member, 5 apps and 5,000 API calls a month.
pros: Complete end-to-end platform with user management and logs
Advanced document segmentation and hybrid search RAG
Active open-source community with frequent updates
cons: Docker Compose deployment requires 4GB+ RAM on host

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.tagline: Framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous AI agents in Python
tools.description: CrewAI enables developers to build collaborative multi-agent teams where each agent has specific roles, backstories, and goals. Perfect for building automated market research, software development, and content pipelines.
tools.pricing_reasoning: The framework is MIT and free to self-host with your own model keys; the hosted AMP free tier allows 2 automations and 50 executions a month.
pros: Clean intuitive Python API for assigning roles and tasks
Seamless support for local Ollama models and cloud APIs
Permissive MIT open-source license
cons: Requires Python programming skills to configure

tools.name: Langflow
tools.tagline: Open-source visual builder for AI agents, RAG pipelines, and API-ready flows
tools.description: Langflow is a low-code visual canvas for building agents, RAG pipelines, and multi-step LLM workflows, with Python code export and an API for every flow. It runs locally via pip or Docker, supports any model provider, and is actively maintained as a successor to Flowise.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed visual builder with no pricing page; you self-host or run the desktop app with your own compute and model keys, and no card is involved.
pros: MIT licensed with a very active community
Visual flows export to deployable Python APIs
Works with local and cloud model providers
cons: Self-hosting requires Docker or Python setup
Large flows need tuning for production scale

tools.name: Activepieces
tools.tagline: Open-source no-code automation with AI steps and hundreds of integrations
tools.description: Activepieces is an MIT-licensed automation platform for building event-driven workflows with AI steps, branching, and hundreds of integrations. Self-hosting is free with unlimited flows, and every piece is open source.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free forever with no card: 1,000 credits a month, unlimited flows and up to 5 users; the core is MIT and can be self-hosted.
pros: MIT licensed with unlimited self-hosted flows
Hundreds of integration pieces
AI steps for LLM-powered automations
cons: Cloud plan is paid; self-hosting is the free route
Fewer community templates than n8n

tools.name: AppFlowy
tools.tagline: Open-source, local-first AI workspace and Notion alternative
tools.description: AppFlowy is an open-source, local-first workspace combining documents, databases, kanban boards, and AI assistants. It runs on your own machine or a self-hosted server, and AI features can use your own model keys.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Personal plan is $0 but capped at 100 MB of storage, 7 MB uploads, one form and one chart, with AI included only as a limited trial.
pros: Local-first data with no mandatory cloud account
Docs, databases, and kanban in one workspace
AGPL-3.0 source available for self-hosting
cons: AI features need a model key or local model
Some polish still trails Notion

tools.name: Scram
tools.tagline: AI web app builder that is free to use and only charges when your app goes live
tools.description: Scram builds apps by assembling pre-tested component blocks instead of generating every line from scratch, which is how it keeps building free: unlimited apps, no credits and no daily caps, subject to fair use. You pay $9 per published app per month, and changes stay free after launch. Built in London by Scram Software — founders George Bevis (Tide) and Tom Godber (Masabi) — and still in beta, so code export, team access and mobile apps are roadmap items rather than shipped features.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Building is $0 with no card, no AI credits and no daily limits for unlimited apps and preview links; publishing costs $9 per app per month.
pros: Unlimited free building with no credits and no daily caps
Only $9 per app per month once you publish to real users
Changes stay free after launch, so iterating costs nothing extra
cons: Publishing, custom domains and collaborators need the paid plan
Beta: no code export, mobile apps or team access yet
Fair-use limits can throttle very heavy AI usage
tools.scope_caveat: Scope note: building and previewing apps is free with no card, but publishing costs $9 per app per month. This is a free prototyping environment, not free hosting.

tools.name: Design Arena
tools.tagline: Free blind A/B arena that ranks AI models on real website, app and design output
tools.description: Design Arena sends one prompt to several frontier models and shows the results head to head with the names hidden until you vote, feeding a public Elo leaderboard. It is free with no paid plans because the preference data is sold to AI labs (built by Arcada Labs, YC S25, $7.9M raised). It is a way to decide which model to pay for, not a builder: there is no code export, and the terms bar commercial use of the service while granting Arcada a broad licence to your prompts and outputs.
tools.pricing_reasoning: The terms state no fees for using the service and there is no pricing page; it is free with no card and no published usage numbers.
pros: Genuinely free with no plan to upgrade to
Blind comparisons remove brand bias before you commit to a subscription
Covers websites, mobile apps, components, images and more
cons: Not a builder: no code export or project handoff
Terms restrict commercial use of the service and outputs
Outputs are public and licensed back to Arcada Labs
tools.scope_caveat: Scope note: Design Arena is a model-comparison benchmark, not a tool you build in. It is listed because it helps you choose a model before paying for one — it cannot export code, host a project or hand work off.

tools.name: Klaviyo
tools.tagline: Email and SMS marketing automation with a permanent free tier
tools.description: Klaviyo is ecommerce-focused email and SMS marketing with flows, segmentation and sign-up forms. The free plan is genuinely indefinite: 250 active profiles, 500 email sends a month, $5 of mobile messages, $5 of its Composer AI agent, plus social marketing, reviews for 50 orders and 10 helpdesk tickets. It is a public company (NYSE: KVYO), so the tier is unlikely to vanish; sending simply pauses when you pass 250 profiles or 500 sends.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan is permanent, not a trial: 250 active profiles, 500 emails a month, $5 of mobile messages and $5 of Composer AI, with no card.
pros: Free forever: 250 active profiles and 500 email sends a month, no card
Flows, segmentation, forms and reporting are included on the free plan
Public company with a mature deliverability and integration ecosystem
cons: Klaviyo branding stays in the email footer and pop-ups on free
No A/B testing until you pay; sending stops at the 250/500 limits
Email support only for the first 60 days; paid email starts at $20/month
tools.scope_caveat: Scope note: Klaviyo is an email and SMS marketing platform, and its free Composer AI is one small part of the free plan. It is listed for AI-assisted flows and copy, not as a general-purpose AI tool or model.

tools.name: Workshop AI
tools.tagline: Agentic app builder with a free tier, four-model Arena mode and a local desktop app
tools.description: Workshop builds websites, dashboards, internal tools and AI apps from a prompt, then publishes them to a *.workshop.build URL. Arena Mode has four models build the same prompt so you can compare the results and pick one, and Agent Mode continues from there; the desktop app adds filesystem access and local open-source models. The free Discover plan needs no card and includes publishing, but keeps free app data for only 10 days and grants 250 credits, so it is a prototyping tier rather than a permanent host.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Discover plan is $0 with no card but the credit allowance is not stated clearly and free app data is kept for only 10 days, so it suits a trial build.
pros: Free Discover plan with no credit card required
Arena Mode compares four models on the same prompt before you commit
Desktop app can run local open-source models for privacy
cons: Free plan keeps app data for only 10 days
250 free credits go quickly; paid plans start at $20/month
No refunds on paid plans and unused credits are forfeited

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.tagline: Open-source coding agent for the terminal, desktop and IDE with 200+ model providers
tools.description: OpenCode is an open-source coding agent that runs in a terminal TUI, a desktop app and editor integrations, and connects to more than 200 model providers as well as local models through Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM. The vendor sells an optional hosted gateway, but the agent works with your own keys or local weights, which is how it stays free.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed agent you run with your own keys or local models; the hosted free models exist but no daily cap is published, so the reliable free path is your own compute or API key.
pros: Open source under MIT, so the agent itself is free forever
Reaches 200+ providers plus local models without lock-in
Terminal, desktop app and editor integrations share one agent
cons: Free hosted models have no published daily cap
The built-in provider needs an account before it appears
Optional paid gateway costs $10/month and up

tools.name: Cline
tools.tagline: Open-source coding agent that lives in your editor and terminal and asks before acting
tools.description: Cline is an AI coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor and Windsurf, with a CLI and a desktop app built on the same agent. It supports bring-your-own-key and local runtimes, and every action it proposes needs your explicit approval before it runs, which makes it easier to supervise than fully autonomous agents.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 extension that is free with your own key or a local runtime; the hosted free models rotate on a limited-time basis with no published quota, so your own credentials are the dependable free route.
pros: Every tool call and file edit waits for your approval
Bring your own key or run a local model with no key at all
Apache-2.0 codebase with editor, CLI and desktop builds
cons: Hosted free models rotate and their quota is not published
Free model usage is unavailable through the Cline API
A $9.99/month pass is needed for higher rate limits

tools.name: Kilo Code
tools.tagline: Open-source agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal with free model routing
tools.description: Kilo Code is an agent that runs across VS Code, JetBrains and a CLI, offering more than 500 models, bring-your-own-key and local model routing. Its free tier routes requests to free models through the Kilo Gateway with no card required, and the client code is MIT licensed.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed clients that work with your own keys or local models; the free Kilo Auto routing requires no card but the vendor publishes no allowance, so it is treated as open source rather than a generous free tier.
pros: Free routing to free models with no credit card
500+ models plus bring-your-own-key and local options
MIT-licensed editor and CLI clients
cons: The free routing allowance is not published
Gateway and cloud backend code is source-available, not MIT
Teams plan is $15 per user per month

tools.name: Qwen Code
tools.tagline: Apache-2.0 terminal coding agent optimised for Qwen models, with any provider you supply
tools.description: Qwen Code is an open-source coding agent for the terminal, with optional editor integration, tuned for the Qwen model family. The vendor free OAuth tier ended in April 2026, so it is now free software rather than a free service: you run it against your own API key, OpenRouter, Fireworks or an Alibaba Cloud coding plan.
tools.pricing_reasoning: The Qwen OAuth free tier was discontinued on 15 April 2026, so the tool is free software rather than a free service: it works with your own key, OpenRouter, Fireworks or a paid Alibaba Cloud plan.
pros: Apache-2.0 agent with no vendor lock-in
Accepts OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini-compatible endpoints
Custom provider support covers local servers and proxies
cons: The vendor free tier ended on 15 April 2026
The route it recommends, Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan Pro, is $50/month
Tuned for Qwen models, so other providers need extra setup

tools.name: Mistral Vibe
tools.tagline: Mistral chat assistant and Apache-2.0 coding CLI in one product, formerly Le Chat
tools.description: Vibe is Mistral single product for chat and code: the web and mobile assistant formerly called Le Chat, plus a coding agent in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal. The CLI is Apache-2.0 and can run against your own Mistral API key, while the hosted assistant has a free plan with limited messages, searches and coding sessions.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan costs $0 with no card and covers chat, search, image editing and limited coding sessions, but Mistral publishes no message or session numbers, so the allowance is limited rather than generous. Pro is $14.99/month for all-day CLI use.
pros: One product covers chat, web search and terminal coding
The CLI is Apache-2.0 and accepts your own API key
Free plan needs no card and includes 100+ connectors
cons: Free limits are described only as limited, with no numbers
All-day coding in the CLI needs the $14.99/month Pro plan
Rebranded from Le Chat, so older guides point at the old name

tools.name: Kimi
tools.tagline: Moonshot AI assistant with agents, slides, sheets and deep research on a free plan
tools.description: Kimi is Moonshot AI assistant, available on the web and as a desktop app, bundling chat, agent tasks, slides, sheets, documents, deep research and scheduled tasks. The free plan needs no card and covers small projects with one concurrent agent task, while Kimi Code and larger limits sit behind paid tiers.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free plan is $0 with no card and states 2 projects, 500 MB project storage, 1 concurrent agent task and 2 scheduled tasks; Kimi Code is excluded, so the allowance is real but small.
pros: Free plan needs no card and includes agents, slides and research
Desktop app alongside the web app
Published free limits rather than vague fair use
cons: Free plan is capped at 2 projects and 500 MB storage
Kimi Code is not available on the free plan
Only 1 concurrent agent task and 2 scheduled tasks

tools.name: Hugging Face Spaces
tools.tagline: Half a million hosted AI demo apps you can use free, with free static hosting
tools.description: Spaces is Hugging Face hosting platform and public directory of AI demo apps built with Gradio, Docker or static pages, running on Hugging Face hardware. Browsing and using public Spaces is free within a daily ZeroGPU allowance, static Spaces can be hosted free, while Gradio and Docker Spaces need paid compute to create.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Free accounts get 5 minutes of ZeroGPU a day (2 unauthenticated minutes) and can host up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces, while Gradio and Docker Spaces need a paid plan to create; static Spaces stay free.
pros: Over 500,000 public AI apps to try without an account
Static Spaces can be hosted for free
Free accounts can keep up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces
cons: Most compute Spaces need a paid plan to create
Free ZeroGPU use is capped at about 5 minutes a day
Dev mode and SSH access require a PRO plan

tools.name: Jan
tools.tagline: Apache-2.0 desktop app that runs local models fully offline with an OpenAI-compatible API
tools.description: Jan is an open-source desktop app for running local language models on Windows, macOS and Linux entirely offline, with no account and no metering. It downloads models from Hugging Face, exposes an OpenAI-compatible server on localhost, and can also connect to cloud providers if you add your own keys.
tools.pricing_reasoning: Apache-2.0 desktop app with no account, no paid tier and no metering; any cost comes from hardware or from cloud model keys you choose to add.
pros: Runs models fully offline with no account required
Apache-2.0 with no paid tier or usage metering
Serves an OpenAI-compatible API on localhost
cons: You supply the model files and the hardware to run them
Cloud models need your own provider keys
Desktop only, with no hosted web version

tools.name: GPT4All
tools.tagline: MIT-licensed local chatbot that runs on your machine and chats with your own documents
tools.description: GPT4All is Nomic free desktop chatbot for Windows, macOS and Ubuntu that runs open-source models locally with no cloud calls, no account and no GPU requirement. LocalDocs adds chat over your own files, and the MIT licence allows commercial use without a paid tier.
tools.pricing_reasoning: MIT-licensed app with direct downloads, no account, no card and no paid tier; local inference is unmetered and the vendor publishes no cap.
pros: MIT licence permits commercial use at no cost
No account, no card and no cloud requests
LocalDocs answers questions about your own files
cons: Desktop only on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu
Larger models need capable local hardware
No hosted fallback if your machine is weak
